seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [reflection,wall] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels x1, no_change x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Single horizontal mirror axis + 3x3-block pieces on a 21x21 block grid; A5 cycles axis->pieces(min block)->axis; A1/A2 move selection by a block, A3/A4 move pieces only.
Moves are blocked by bounds, the axis row and other pieces; reflections are piece blocks mirrored to 2A-r (clipped, not on pieces); targets are static solid blocks.
Frame = layered composite wall<target<reflection<piece: first solid wins, else topmost hole fill (selected 0, reflection 4), then re-extracted per type; wall index counts non-wall 0 pixels.
Hypothesis resolved: target A1 h,pixels change vs no_change = whether the moved reflection newly occludes the target (reflection layer 3 > target 2), not a target field.
Unconfirmed: piece cycle order beyond the first piece, ACTION6/7 (no-ops). Passes 30/30 with hidden state disabled too.
